title: Members of Congress Increasingly Take Jobs as AI Lobbyists
author: Lee Fang
content:

Senator Kyrsten Sinema, the independent U.S. Senator from Arizona who retired
last year after leaving the Democratic Party, filmed an infomercial for her
new position as a senior advisor at law and lobbying powerhouse Hogan Lovells.

"I was really drawn to to the firm for its incredible ability to help clients
at the intersection of business and government," Sinema says in the video.
Moments later, [she exclaims](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TjE-Qs1o9bU)
that she is "excited to start working with companies" and singles out those
involved in artificial intelligence.

In Silicon Valley, AI tech giants are in a [bidding
war](https://www.entrepreneur.com/business-news/meta-makes-billion-dollar-job-
offer-competing-for-ai-talent/495672), competing to hire the best and
brightest computer programmers. But a different hiring spree is underway in
D.C.

AI firms are on an influence-peddling spree, hiring hundreds of former
government officials and retaining former members of Congress as consultants
and lobbyists. The latest disclosure filings show over 500 entities lobbying
on AI policy--from federal rules designed to preempt state and local safety
regulations to water and energy-intensive data centers and integration into
government contracting and certifications.

Lawmakers are increasingly making the jump from serving constituents as
elected officials to working directly as influence peddlers for AI interests.

- Former **Sen. Laphonza Butler, D-Calif.** , a [former lobbyist](https://www.leefang.com/p/governor-newsom-selects-political) appointed to the U.S. Senate to fill the seat of Sen. Dianne Feinstein, left Congress last year and returned to her former profession. She is now working as a consultant to OpenAI, the firm behind ChatGPT.  
  
- Former **Sen. Richard Burr, R-N.C.** , recently [registered](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/af39c4c4-8f15-4604-86f7-36550e6ec326/print/) for the first time as a lobbyist. Among his initial clients is ​Lazarus AI, which sells AI products to the Defense Department.  
  
- OpenAI also registered former **Rep. Cheri Bustos, D-Ill.** , a former senior ranking Democrat, as a lobbyist via the firm Mercury LLC. Bustos's [disclosure](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/ee2b9386-0545-4d2c-92f0-a1542ff1122c/print/) notes she works on "issues related to artificial intelligence policy" on behalf of the firm.

- Former **Rep Kevin Yoder, R-Kansas** , is registered to lobby on AI policy for [Microsoft](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/e44324c7-9249-488c-b376-9e6ea9babc68/print/) and [BigBear.AI](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/3cae6d25-1ca8-419e-b7df-15f453a0c209/print/), which he is working to shape policies "impacting AI-powered decision intelligence solutions for defense, national security, travel & transportation."

- Former **Rep. William Lacy Clay, D-Mo.** , is [registered](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/3636b4c3-87ed-4b35-bb59-29596b9b54b6/print/) to lobby for Windward USA to a leading maritime AI company, to influence AI policy.  
  
- Former **Rep. Chris Stewart, R-Utah** , is registered to lobby on AI policy for firms [Polygraf AI](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/c34577b5-4b51-4e14-bc53-f3b44a31541b/print/) and [Virtualitics, Inc.  
  
](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/487d1769-b0f9-4698-bc48-22f1beac6bcb/print/)-
Former **Sen. Norm Coleman, R-MN** , was previously registered to lobby on
behalf of OpenAI. He is [currently
registered](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/f4b60808-9fcc-4bf3-b5ca-b6f10e520ac9/print/)
to represent the Computer & Communications Industry Association, a trade group
for Amazon, Apple, and Google, among other major tech firms. Coleman works for
CCIA's "Don't Break What Works campaign," which fights to stop anti-monopoly
legislation such as the American Innovation and Choice Act. The campaign
[claims efforts](https://dontbreakwhatworks.ccianet.org/resources/congress-
should-preserve-american-ai-innovation/) to break up tech monopolies will harm
"American AI innovation."  
  
- Former **Rep. Jeff Miller, R-Fla**., [represents](https://lda.senate.gov/filings/public/filing/620e2033-cefe-41ac-a147-c7d5a363d3e7/print/) data and AI giant Palantir as a registered lobbyist through his work at the Trump-connected firm Ballard Partners.

The expanding reach of artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping hundreds
of professions, weapons of war, and the ways we connect with one another. The
technology, many predict, will serve a transformative role akin to another
industrial revolution.

How will Americans cope with the changes as industries as diverse as trucking
and copyediting are replaced en masse by AI-powered automation?

The pace and scale of the leap are yet to be seen. What's clear is that the AI
firms set to benefit most from these changes are taking control of the
policymaking apparatus to write the laws and regulations during the
transition.
